# Additions to Esther Chapter 3 (Addition C) — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther C
**Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_003_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Decision

This is the most important passage in Greek Esther. Two competing demands are in tension: (1) the prayers must preserve the gravity and address-form of biblical prayer literature; (2) Esther's prayer in particular is startlingly personal, bodily, and raw. The council rules that both demands must be honored. LOGOS provides the base structure for Mordecai's prayer (vv. 1–10); PNEUMA's voice dominates Esther's prayer (vv. 14–31), especially her confessions at vv. 27–30, which must be rendered honestly and without softening.

The decision on v.28: "I abhor the sign of my arrogance... like a cloth of menstruation" is retained verbatim. LOGOS's "cloth of menstruation" is adopted; PNEUMA's "the way you hate" is interpretive and dropped. EMET's literal "sign of my arrogance" is adopted over LOGOS's "sign of my pride" since ὑπερηφανίας is strong.

---

*[Addition C: Prayers of Mordecai and Esther. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 4:17.]*

**1** Then Mordecai prayed to the Lord, calling to mind all the works of the Lord, and said:

**2** "O Lord, Lord, almighty King — all things are subject to your power, and there is no one who can stand against you when it is your will to save Israel.

**3** For you made the heaven and the earth and every wonderful thing under heaven.

**4** You are Lord over all, and there is none who can withstand you, O Lord.

**5** You know all things. And Lord, you know this: it was not from insolence or pride or vainglory that I acted as I did — refusing to bow down to the arrogant Haman.

**6** I would gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for the sake of the salvation of Israel.

**7** But I did this so that I would not set the honor of a man above the honor of God; and I will bow to no one but you, who are my God and my Lord; and I will not act out of pride.

**8** And now, O Lord, God and King, God of Abraham — have compassion on your people. Their eyes are fixed on us to destroy us; they want to annihilate the inheritance that has been yours from the very beginning.

**9** Do not abandon your own portion, which you redeemed for yourself out of the land of Egypt.

**10** Hear my prayer and be merciful to your inheritance. Turn our mourning into celebration, so that we may live and praise your name, O Lord. Do not close the mouths of those who praise you, O Lord."

**11** And all Israel cried out with great force, for death was before them.

**12** And Queen Esther was seized with anguish. She fled to the Lord.

**13** She stripped off her splendid garments and put on garments of grief and mourning. In place of costly perfumes she covered her head with ashes and dung, and she greatly humbled her body. Every place she had adorned with joy she filled with the wild tangles of her unbound hair.

**14** And she prayed to the Lord God of Israel, saying:

**15** "O my Lord, you alone are our King. Help me — I am alone, and I have no helper but you.

**16** My danger is immediate.

**17** From my childhood I heard it in my father's family: you, O Lord, chose Israel out of all the nations, and chose our ancestors out of all their forebears, as an everlasting inheritance; and you kept for them everything you promised.

**18** But now we have sinned before you, and you have handed us over to our enemies

**19** because we gave glory to their gods. You are righteous, O Lord.

**20** Yet they are still not satisfied with the bitterness of our slavery; they have joined hands with their idols

**21** to abolish the decree that came from your own mouth — to destroy your inheritance, to silence the mouths of those who praise you, to extinguish the glory of your house and your altar,

**22** and to open the mouths of the nations in praise of empty idols, and to magnify a mortal king forever.

**23** Do not hand over your scepter, O Lord, to things that have no existence. Do not let them make sport of our ruin. Turn their own counsel against them. Make an example of the man who first moved against us.

**24** Remember us, O Lord. Make yourself known in the time of our tribulation. Give me courage, O King of the gods and Master of all dominion.

**25** Put persuasive speech in my mouth before the lion. Turn his heart so that he hates the one fighting against us, so that there may be an end to him and all those who agree with him.

**26** Deliver us by your own hand. Help me — I am alone, and have no helper but you, O Lord.

**27** You know all things, and you know this: I hate the glory of the lawless. I abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of every foreigner.

**28** You know my constraint. I abhor the sign of my arrogance upon my head on the days when I must appear in public. I abhor it like a cloth of menstruation, and I do not wear it on my days of quiet.

**29** And your servant has not eaten at the table of Haman. I have not honored the feasts of the king. I have not drunk the wine of libations.

**30** And from the day I was brought here until this moment, your servant has known no joy — only in you, O Lord God of Abraham.

**31** O God, mighty above all, hear the voice of the despairing. Save us from the hand of the wicked, and deliver me from my fear."
